summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who peeped through the door of his room, saying that seeking permission exists to protect the sight.
Abu Sa'eed Khudri describes how Abu Moosa, refused entry three times by Umar, left, and how Umar demanded a witness before Ubay bin Ka'b and Abu Sa'eed confirmed the Prophet's ruling.
notes: The source says 'Abu Sa'eed Khudri or Abu Mas'ood' accompanied Abu Moosa; the second companion is tagged abu-masood-ansaari on the strength of the name, but the source itself is unsure which of the two went. Sa'd bin Ubaadah appears in the story of the Prophet's greetings, which is quoted here.

summary: Abu Moosa recounts that the Ansaar confirmed the rule of seeking permission three times, after which Umar accepted the testimony of Abu Sa'eed or Abu Mas'ood and of Sa'd bin Ubaadah about the Prophet's greetings.
notes: Continues the report in n01762 ('Another adds'). The Abu Sa'eed or Abu Mas'ood ambiguity is as in the source.

summary: Aamir bin Abdullaah reports that Umar refused a slave girl entry and sent after her, and that Hudhayfah warned a man who asked whether he must seek permission even from his mother.
notes: Hudhayfah is given without a father's name. The vocab has Hudhayfa bin Yamaan and Hudhayfa bin Mihsin; the text does not say which, so this is left unmatched. The daughter of 'Hadhrat (RA)' is unnamed in the OCR and omitted.

summary: Suwayd Abdi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar questioned him about peeping into his room, and that when asked about Jihaad, Abdullaah answered that whoever wages Jihaad does so for his own benefit.

Baraa bin Aazib reports that the Prophet named loving and hating for Allaah's sake as the strongest link of Imaan, and Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying the same deed is the most beloved to Allaah.
new_themes: loving for the sake of Allaah
notes: Two reports: Baraa bin Aazib's account, then 'another narration' from Abu Dharr.

summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet loved the people of taqwa, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells Abu Dharr he loves him for Allaah's sake, which the Prophet called rewarding.
new_themes: loving for the sake of Allaah
notes: The opening is lost in the OCR ('that he had not, Rasulullaah told him to do so'). The man who met Abu Dharr is not named in the surviving text; he is taken as Abdullaah bin Mas'ood because the text then says 'Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) reported back'. Ammaar is in the heading only and is left out.

summary: Mujaahid reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas said a passing man liked him a lot, and explained that he liked the man in return.
new_themes: loving for the sake of Allaah
notes: Mujaahid is not in the vocab. sahabi 'no' comes from general knowledge (he is a Tabi'i), not from the book.

summary: Mujaahid reports a Sahabi who told him he loved him for Allaah's sake and offered his daughter in marriage, and then reports Abdullaah bin Umar's saying that friendships and enmities must be for Allaah's sake.
new_themes: loving for the sake of Allaah
notes: Two reports: the Sahabi's account (with the Prophet's saying about telling a person you love him) and Abdullaah bin Umar's statement. The Sahabi is unnamed and left out.

summary: Auf bin Tufayl reports that Aa'isha vowed never to speak to Abdullaah bin Zubayr after he remarked on her charity, until Miswar and Abdur Rahmaan brought about reconciliation; Urwa bin Zubayr adds that she freed forty slaves as expiation.

people.name: Abdur Rahmaan bin Aswad bin Abd Yaghooth

notes: Two reports: Auf bin Tufayl's account and Urwa bin Zubayr's account. Tufayl is Aa'isha's uterine brother and Auf's father. Abdur Rahmaan is given RA in the text, so sahabi is yes. A Tabraani citation and footnote markers are OCR debris and were ignored.

summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the people of Quba fell into a dispute that led to stone-throwing, and that the Prophet went to settle it; another report says the same of the Banu Amr bin Auf.
notes: The text ends 'The Hadith continues further.' It also contains a second, variant report about the Banu Amr bin Auf tribe.

summary: Anas reports that Abdullaah bin Ubay insulted the Prophet's donkey, the two sides quarrelled and fought, and the Prophet calmed them; Anas says this is the occasion of the revelation on reconciling believers.
notes: A cross-reference to Usaamah's report, which the text says appears in another chapter, is not part of this narration and is left out.

summary: Anas reports that the Aws and the Khazraj, who had been enemies, fought over a quarrel of poetry, and that the Prophet stopped them by reciting the verses on unity and the fear of Allaah.
notes: The Aws and Khazraj are tribes and the Ansaar are unnamed, so none are tagged.

summary: Haaroon bin Rabaab reports that Abdullaah bin Amr, on his deathbed, asked people to find a man to whom he had promised his daughter and married her to him, so as not to meet Allaah with a broken promise.
notes: The man to whom the daughter was promised is unnamed and left out. Trailing OCR debris after the statement was ignored.

summary: Anas reports that a Sahabi disliked a passing man, and after questioning the man's neighbour and the Sahabi, the Prophet said the man was the better of the two.
notes: The Sahabi who made the remark, the man, and the neighbour are unnamed and left out.

summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports that a man from the Banu Layth asked the Prophet's permission three times, then recited a poem praising the Prophet, and the Prophet approved it.
Khallaad bin Saa'ib reports that Usaamah bin Zaid praised him to his face, explaining that the Prophet said praise given to a believer's face increases his Imaan.
The father of Mutarrif reports that a delegation from the Banu Aamir praised the Prophet, and he told them to speak more simply and not overstep the limits of praise.
notes: The narrator is named only as the father of Mutarrif, so his name is not recorded. The Banu Aamir are a tribe and are not tagged.

summary: Another narration says the Prophet asked not to be raised above the rank Allaah gave him, describing himself as the servant of Allaah and His Rasul.
notes: A continuation of the Prophet's speech in n01778; no narrator is named.

summary: Anas reports that someone called the Prophet the best of people and the son of the best, and the Prophet corrected him to say only what he was told and to keep to the limits Allaah set.
notes: The speaker is unnamed and left out.

summary: Abu Bakrah reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who praised another in front of him, and taught that one should say only that he believes a person to be righteous, since only Allaah knows.
Abu Moosa reports that the Prophet, hearing someone overstate his praise for another, told him that he had broken the man's back.
notes: The text is cut off mid-sentence after 'for'.

summary: Rajaa reports that Buraydah Aslami joked to Mihjin Aslami about the long prayer of Sabkah, and that the Prophet forbade Mihjin from praising the man in his hearing and said the best deed of the religion is the easiest.
notes: Buraydah Aslami is matched to buraydah-bin-husayb (the Aslami nisba). The vocab also lists buraydah-bin-khusayb (yes), which may be the same person; please check. Rajaa is not in the vocab.

summary: Another report from Rajaa says the Prophet told Mihjin to stop praising the worshipper, repeated that the best deed of the religion is the easiest, and said Allaah wants ease for this nation.
notes: Several variant reports are run together: the Prophet's words, a further report that Mihjin praised the man as the best of Madinah, and the closing words on ease. The variant on Mihjin's praise has the Prophet speaking twice or thrice.

summary: Ibraheem Taymi reports that Umar rebuked a man who praised another to his face, saying he had slaughtered him and asking how one can praise a man's Deen to his face.
notes: The father from whom Ibraheem reports, and the person who praised the man, are unnamed and left out.

summary: Hasan reports that when someone praised Umar, Umar said the praiser was destroying both himself and Umar.
notes: The text does not say which Hasan this is. It could be Hasan bin Ali (yes) or Hasan al-Basri (no); left unmatched rather than guessed.

summary: Hasan reports that Umar struck Jaarood with a whip after a remark that Jaarood was the leader of the Rabee'ah, explaining that he wanted to remove any pride that might settle in Jaarood's heart.
notes: The text is cut off mid-sentence ('remove the effect from'). Hasan is unmatched, as in n01786.

summary: Hammaam reports that Miqdaad threw pebbles in the face of a man praising Uthmaan, quoting the Prophet's command to throw sand at those who praise for ulterior motives.
notes: The text is cut off after 'in their'. Hammaam is matched by name only (the vocab has no parentage for him). The praiser is unnamed. The text says pebbles, so the summary follows the text rather than the sand of the chapter heading.

summary: Another narration says Miqdaad threw sand on the face of a man who was heaping praise on one of the Khalifahs, citing the Prophet's command.
notes: Narrator not named. The Khalifah and the man who praised him are unnamed.

summary: Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports that Abdullaah bin Umar threw sand at the mouth of a man who praised another in his presence, quoting the Prophet's instruction.
notes: Near-duplicate of n01791, which has Abdullaah bin Umar being praised himself.

summary: Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports that Abdullaah bin Umar threw sand at the mouth of a man who praised Abdullaah himself, citing the Prophet's words.
notes: Variant of n01790.

summary: Naafi reports that when someone called Abdullaah bin Umar the best of people, Abdullaah replied that he was only a servant of Allaah, and that people keep praising a man until they destroy him.
notes: The text says 'Naafi and other' reported this; the second transmitter is not named.

summary: Taariq bin Shihaab reports that Abdullaah bin Umar warned that a man can leave home with his Deen intact and return without it after swearing praise of a powerless man in the hope of gain.
notes: The text is cut off after 'because'. Taariq bin Shihaab is unsure in the vocab and is used as listed.

summary: Sa'd bin Hishaam reports that when he asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, she replied that his character was the Qur'aan.
notes: The sentence lacks a closing bracket but reads as complete.

summary: Qataadah says the Qur'aan brought every noble trait, and Abu Dardaa reports that Aa'isha described the Prophet's character as the Qur'aan, being pleased with what Allaah is pleased with.
notes: Two reports: Qataadah's statement and Abu Dardaa's report. The text gives Qataadah as (RA), but the vocab lists id qataada as no; the id is used as listed but the RA conflict should be checked.

summary: Zaid bin Baabnoos reports that when people asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, she told them to read from Surah Mu'minoon and said that was his character.
notes: The people who asked are unnamed and left out.

summary: Aa'isha says there was none with better character than the Prophet, and the report goes on to a garbled account of his dealings with the Jews of Khaybar.
notes: The narrator's name is lost in the OCR ('Hadhrat (RA) reports'). The text is garbled and cut off, so the second half of the summary is not certain. The Jews of Khaybar are a group and are not tagged.

summary: Anas reports that the Prophet was the most compassionate of people, never refusing a slave or child who brought him water, listening patiently to requests, and never withdrawing his hand before the other person did.
Anas bin Maalik reports that the slaves of Madinah brought water to the Prophet after Fajr, and he dipped his hands into every vessel for blessing, even on very cold mornings.
Anas reports that the Prophet never withdrew his hand or turned away from a person until that person did, and never moved his head from one whispering to him until the person moved away.
notes: Two paragraphs, each a separate report from Anas. The text is also cut off at the very end ('Rasulullaah's').
